name: Iowa
agency: Iowa Department of Transportation (Motor Vehicle Division)
permitAge: 14 (instruction permit), with parent or guardian consent, vision screening and knowledge test (Iowa Code 321.180B; secondary sources)

teen.supervisedHours: 20 hours, including at least 2 between sunset and sunrise; driver education driving counts (Iowa DOT)
teen.holdPermit: 12 months in total before the intermediate license at 16, plus a clean record for the last 6 consecutive months (Iowa DOT)
teen.nightLimit: Intermediate license: no driving without adult supervision 12:30 a.m. to 5 a.m.; parent can file a waiver (form 431170) for school or work, carried in the vehicle (Iowa Code 321.180B, Iowa DOT)
teen.passengerLimit: Intermediate license, first 6 months: no more than one unrelated passenger under 18 unless supervised; siblings and household children do not count (Iowa Code 321.180B as amended 2013; current text not re-checked)
teen.phone: Permit and intermediate holders: no electronic communication or entertainment device while driving, except equipment permanently installed (Iowa DOT). All drivers: hand-held ban since July 1, 2025; fines from January 2026 (UI Injury Prevention Research Center).

notes: Permit supervisor: licensed immediate family member at least 21, a certified driver education instructor, or a licensed person at least 25 with written parent permission (Iowa Code 321.180B).
Minor school license (special minor’s restricted license): from 14 1/2, driver education, permit plus 6 clean months, usually living 1 mile or more from school (Iowa DOT MM690 card).
Knowledge test: third-party sites agree on 80 percent but disagree on the number of questions (25 vs 35); not confirmed by Iowa DOT, so questions and pass are null.

Move Over or Slow Down (Iowa Code 321.323A): change lanes or slow down for stationary emergency, tow, maintenance, construction or solid waste vehicles with flashing lights, and any stationary vehicle with hazard lights (Iowa DOT).

School bus: on roads with 2 or more lanes each way, opposite-direction traffic need not stop; on roads with 3 lanes or fewer every vehicle stops, including turning lanes (KWQC citing Iowa DOT). Suspension up to 180 days for failing to stop.
Speed: 20 mph business district default (Iowa Code 321.285); 70 mph on rural interstates (secondary sources).

Handbook URLs: English address iowadot.gov/driversmanual is quoted inside the Spanish manual; Spanish PDF at iowadot.gov/media/7173/download (edition not confirmed). Archive copies at publications.iowa.gov (English 52007, Spanish 42618). Whether the test is offered in Spanish was not found.
